37.9.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa By the breath of God frost (ice) is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened [10].

37.9.1.en: The falling of ice (frozen water) is permitted. Although the appearance of ice results from natural causes, even these phenomena do not occur at random, but God is the Controller of nature. The Psalmist says: “He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes. He casteth forth his ice (his snow) like morsels: who can stand before his cold?” (Ps 147:16-17).

37.9.2.en: * Who is it who pours out the air in such great abundance...? He does not supply it by measures according to the rank of men and their wealth, nor is it bounded by certain limits, nor does He divide it according to the ages of the people, but as He used to distribute the manna (Ex 16:18), He supplies enough for all equally; and the winged chariot of creation, and the seat of the winds, and the intermediate seasons of the year, and the Giver of life to living beings, or rather the Preserver of the natural life of the body, by which bodies live and by which they speak, and in which is the light and all that shines upon it, and the sight that pours forth through it...? What are the storehouses of the winds? What are the treasures of the snow...? And as Scripture says: Who begot the drops of dew? From whose womb came the snow? And who binds the water in the clouds, and fixes the parts of the clouds...

37.9.3.en: * [When God breathes, the ice is frozen] [10]. When the Holy Spirit breathes on the hearts of believers and grants the wonders of great power, the flesh grows that causes paralysis (numbness) in the dullness of the hearts of unbelievers. The unbelieving multitudes become hardened against God by the very causes that make the humble people cease from the stubbornness to which they were bound. For when God breathes on them, those became ice, as they said through their envy of the miracles He wrought: “behold, the world is gone after him” (Jn 12:19). They saw the signs, and recognized the miracles wrought by His servants, and had already seen the whole world go to follow the preaching of the faith. Yet the more the Holy Spirit filled the world, the more they clung to the malice of envy that binds their minds.

37.9.4.en: [And He pours out the water in abundance]. For the Lord truly pours out the waters in abundance after this ice. After He bore the hardness of the Jews, after His death, He at once melted their hearts from the hardness of their unbelief, breathing upon them the breath of love toward Him, so that they ran to Him eagerly to obey Him, as far as possible, as the wise man says: [As the ice in fair weather, so shall your sins melt away and be taken from you] (see Sir 3:17)...

37.9.5.en: Of the waters, that is, the people gathered together toward the Lord, it is said: “He sendeth out his word, and melteth them: he causeth his wind (his breath) to blow, and the waters flow” (Ps 147:18).

37.9.6.en: Was not Paul ice as he was going to Damascus, after he had received letters, and was working against the seeds of the word of God that had been scattered in the hearts of believers as in the earth, so that they might not sprout and reach the perfection of good works? But this ice was turned to water, and was afterwards watered by the streams of holy counsels, those whom he had formerly sought to press down by persecution. This was so that they might bring a plentiful harvest for the elect, to the extent that God’s rains from the mouth of the persecutor watered them.

37.9.7.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud.

37.10.0.en: he scattereth the cloud of his light [11].

37.10.1.en: When the Lord waters the earth He empties the thick cloud so that it pours rain on the earth, that it may sprout and buds may appear. In the Septuagint: “The wheat asks for a cloud.”

37.10.2.en: “He scattereth the cloud of his light.” Some see that God in His love makes the dense clouds like a pregnant woman who suffers pain as she gives birth to a child. The dense clouds bring rains and are dispersed, as though they bear pains for the service of man and the watering of the earth for him.

37.10.3.en: When the rains fall, the clouds become light and bright.

37.11.0.en: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth [12].

37.11.1.en: The clouds seem to revolve upon themselves at random. God moves the clouds according to His pleasure, and they obey Him and go from one place to another on the face of the earth. The clouds have no ability to move as they please, but the will of the Creator is carried out.

37.11.2.en: If the movements of the clouds need divine guidance, how much more does mankind need this guidance. The wise man says: “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety” (Prov 11:14). “Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war” (Prov 20:18).

37.11.3.en: The Psalmist tells us of the submission of nature with all its phenomena to God, saying: “Fire, and hail; snow, and vapours; stormy wind fulfilling his word” (Ps 148:8).

37.12.0.en: Whether it be for correction, or for his land, or for mercy, he causeth it to come [13].

37.12.1.en: The movements of nature, such as the clouds laden with rain that seem random, are by God’s permission, either for correction, or as a sign of God’s favor toward man, or out of His tenderness and mercy upon him.

37.12.2.en: He sometimes permits storms and floods for correction, as happened in the ancient world (Gen 7:11-12).

37.12.3.en: “For his land”: when God sends rain on the earth as a sign of His favor and delight in man, He regards the earth as His own land. The Psalmist says: “The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein” (Ps 24:1).

37.12.4.en: The text in the Vulgate reads: “Whether in one tribe, or in his land, or in whatever land, according to His mercy He sends it.” If the storms and the clouds full of rain move according to His pleasure, He also determines for them the place where they blow or fall.

37.12.5.en: By saying “for his land” God wishes to affirm that He longs for man to live as in the Lord’s land, as though He raises from him another Adam dwelling in the garden of God, which He plants with His hands and waters with the waters of His grace, to bear joyful and delightful fruits for the godly man.

37.13.s.en: 3. Job, a judge unqualified to judge God’s providence

37.13.0.en: 14 “Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God. 15 Dost thou know God’s attention to them, or the shining of the light of his cloud? 16 Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge? 17 How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind? 18 Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass? 19 Teach us what we shall say unto him; for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness. 20 Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up. 21 And now men see not the bright light which is in the sky: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth it. 22 Out of the north cometh gold: with God is terrible majesty.”

37.13.1.en: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God [14].

37.13.2.en: Elihu invites Job to turn his gaze from the afflictions that have come upon him and driven him to murmur, and to consider earnestly the wondrous works of God and His surpassing works for believers. By this his mind and heart are filled with love for God and he perceives His divine care, and his soul finds rest within him. The Psalmist says: “The works of the LORD are great, sought out of all them that have pleasure therein” (Ps 111:2).

37.14.0.en: Dost thou know God’s attention to them, or the shining of the light of his cloud [15].

37.14.1.en: Elihu asks: Can man grasp how God moves the storms, clouds, rains and so on, and how He brings forth shining lightning from dark, gloomy clouds?

37.15.0.en: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge [16].

37.15.1.en: Who knows how the clouds are suspended in the air in a wonderful balance, how they are formed from evaporated water and gather together in the air, and remain floating in a certain place for a certain time, as though a hidden hand held and kept them, and then fall as rains to water the earth. They reveal a great and perfect wisdom!

37.15.2.en: With all that science and knowledge have attained, we can account for these phenomena, but they are not under man’s authority, and he is unable to grasp all their secrets exactly.

37.16.0.en: How thy garments are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south wind [17].

37.16.1.en: How does man explain that his body becomes warm when the warm south winds blow, and even the clothes become warm?

37.16.2.en: We saw in the Song of Songs how the bride asks that the north wind and also the south wind blow upon her, so that her inner garden gives forth the joyful fruits of the Spirit (Song 4:16).

37.16.3.en: Some see that Elihu puts this question in a sarcastic way, for it is among the simplest things that clothes become warm when warm winds blow, yet man offers no exact explanation of this phenomenon.

37.17.0.en: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a molten looking glass? [18]

37.17.1.en: He asks him: Did you spread out with God the strong sky of heaven like a molten mirror? Were you with God when He made the breadth of the winds and their extent in proportion to their weight?

37.17.2.en: Do you not see how the heaven, when it is clear, is like a huge, strong molten mirror?

37.17.3.en: Here he speaks of the sky of heaven as a mirror. Scripture also speaks of it as like a tent or a curtain: “It is he that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain (as a veil), and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in” (Isa 40:22). And also as a scroll: “And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree” (Isa 34:4). And sometimes as a garment: [The heavens are the work of thy hands. They shall perish, but thou shalt endure: yea, all of them shall wax old like a garment; as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed] (Ps 102:25-26).

37.17.4.en: “Strong,” so that it supports itself by itself.

37.17.5.en: Teach us what we shall say unto him;

37.18.0.en: for we cannot order our speech by reason of darkness! [19]

37.18.1.en: Elihu invites Job to pay attention to the thunder, which symbolizes the voice of God and expresses the greatness of God. In humility Elihu declares that man’s mind is exceedingly dark, unable to enter into dispute with the great God, and if he does so let him expect his destruction [19-20].

37.18.2.en: Since Elihu feels great awe toward God, he asks Job to teach him what to say to the awesome God, what words he can utter in the face of God’s greatness.

37.18.3.en: Job often repeated his plea to enter into a trial with God and to touch the divine presence in order to complain to Him of his condition. So Elihu advises him not to ask this, for the words will flee from his lips when he stands before the majesty of the great God.

37.18.4.en: It is as though he says to him: “You seem to be very wise, and to have complete knowledge about God; grant us to be wise like you, so that we may be able to approach God and speak with Him, for we feel as though we were wrapped in darkness. For our part we confess our ignorance and helplessness; tell us and teach us how to stand to argue with Him!” Or it is as though he says to him: “Men cannot explain God’s wonders and grasp their secrets, and so we cannot enter into a quarrel with Him. Teach us how we can do this?”

37.18.5.en: Shall it be told him that I speak?

37.19.0.en: if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up [20].

37.19.1.en: He says: Can I dare to whisper in the presence of God? And if someone should speak against me and accuse me before Him because of what I have said, even if he made the accusation with sincere intent, how could I dare to stand in His presence? For I would be swallowed up by terror, and perish at the loftiness of His majesty.

37.19.2.en: If anyone dares to speak what does not befit the majesty of God, that is, if he is a murmurer, he is utterly swallowed up!

37.20.0.en: And now men see not the bright light which is in the sky: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth it [21].

37.20.1.en: If God’s greatness is now hidden, it will surely be suddenly revealed at some time in the fullness of its splendor, when the darkness is scattered from Job’s eyes. This is as happens with the sun, whose rays are hidden behind the cloud, but as soon as the winds blow and scatter the clouds its splendor appears.

37.20.2.en: So it is fitting for the believer whose eyes are veiled by trials from seeing the splendor of God’s glory, His righteousness and His justice, to wait in patience and longsuffering, for the Holy Spirit will blow upon him, removing from him the cloud of darkness, and he will see what had been hidden from his eyes.

37.20.3.en: Since the storm had indeed begun, Elihu asks Job to wait patiently, for the time was near when God would reveal Himself to him in His splendor and speak with him, after the winds drive away the cloud of trials that darkened his eyes.

37.20.4.en: Some see that Elihu here refers to man’s inability to see the sun in its splendor once the winds blow and the sky becomes clear of clouds; how then can he ask to see God face to face to present his complaint before Him? Instead it is fitting for him to bow down before Him, submitting to Him in a spirit of humility, instead of murmuring and speaking with God as one who accuses Him.

37.20.5.en: God declares Himself as a passing cloud that leaves the light of the sun very bright, which can be seen in the splendor of His glory that surrounds us [21-22].

37.20.6.en: Out of the north cometh gold:

37.21.1.en: In the Septuagint: “The clouds shine like gold.”

37.21.2.en: When Elihu saw the storm coming from the north, he explained that the clouds coming with the storm flash like pure, shining gold as a symbol of God’s approach.

37.21.3.en: St. Augustine sees that the north points to the city of the Gentiles, while Zion is in the south, and that the devil ruled the north, where he says: “I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north” (Isa 14:12-13). When the Gentiles accept faith in the Lord Christ, they leave the kingdom of the devil and are freed from it, and they come from the north, having become gold, that is, having become kings, enlightened by grace in Christ Jesus; they have become a golden cloud.

37.22.s.en: 4. God is perfect, great and awesome

37.22.0.en: 23 “Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: he is great in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not answer. 24 Men do therefore fear him: he regardeth not any that are wise of heart.”

37.22.1.en: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out:

37.22.2.en: he is great in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice.

37.22.4.en: Even if God draws near to Job through a visible splendor surrounded by clouds and storms and sits on a throne of polished gold, yet, in Elihu’s opinion, it is impossible for anyone to grasp God, for His greatness is exceedingly surpassing, His power is unlimited, and so are His justice and His righteousness. And it is fitting for Job to know beforehand that God’s appearing to him does not mean that He will answer his questions, for it is not the right of the creature to interrogate God, since it is unable to grasp His wisdom.

37.23.0.en: he regardeth not any that are wise of heart [24].

37.23.1.en: It is fitting for men, when they meet God, to confess that they are sinners, ignorant and wretched, fearing the Holy and Wise One alone.

37.23.2.en: God does not show favor to a man as one who is wise in his own eyes, for what wisdom can be ascribed to any man when compared with God, who is all-wise and all-knowing? What goodness can be ascribed to him when compared with the One alone who is holy?

37.23.3.en: Thus Elihu concludes his speech in a manner entirely different from the three friends. He concludes it by highlighting God’s greatness, majesty, wisdom and power, before which it is fitting for every man, whatever his ability and gifts, to submit in contrition.

37.23.4.en: He concluded his speech by saying that he sees the divine majesty drawing near to meet Job like a cloud of bright, polished gold, and he wants Job to prepare for this meeting by ceasing from murmuring and complaint, and by confessing God’s great works, His justice and His righteousness.

37.23.5.en: Elihu sees that the Lord is coming, and it is fitting that all human speech and dispute cease, that all submit in silence and listen to the divine voice.

37.23.6.en: It is enough for us to be convinced that He acts with justice [23-24].

37.23.7.en: May Your voice thunder in my heart!

37.23.8.en: * Let the storm of Your love blow in my depths, and let Your voice thunder in my heart!

37.23.9.en: No one can change my depths except the voice of Your love.

37.23.10.en: And no one gives me Your awesome fear, filled with sweetness, except Your voice.

37.23.11.en: The thunder of Your voice shakes my whole being. It shatters all corruption within me, and separates my soul from all temporal concerns.

37.23.12.en: In sweet awe my mind is lifted to the throne of Your grace, and my intellect is absorbed in Your majesty!

37.23.13.en: I long never to part from You until I depart from this world.

37.23.14.en: * The thunder of Your voice breaks the lofty cedars, and uproots from me all pride.

37.23.15.en: The clouds of Your love rain on the earth of my heart, and turn it into a joyful heavenly garden.

37.23.16.en: It bears the surpassing fruits of the Spirit.

37.23.17.en: * In the midst of this dense cloud You flash suddenly.

37.23.18.en: I see the rays of Your lights for moments, and my soul is enlightened by You, and I come to know Your secrets.

37.23.19.en: Your light cools every darkness in me, and turns my darkness into radiant light!

37.23.20.en: * The waters of the rains turn into dazzling white snow.

37.23.21.en: My heart, covered by the snow, becomes utterly pure!

37.23.22.en: My soul praises You, for You scatter my sins and take them away, and my soul is filled with the snow of Your radiant wisdom.

37.23.23.en: * The enemy of good, the ravenous beast, makes every effort to break into Your garden in me.

37.23.24.en: He will not be able to come near as long as You are within me.

37.23.25.en: And if he deceives me and enters, he will not settle, for Your grace drives him out quickly!

37.23.26.en: Yes, keep Your garden from this wicked enemy!

37.23.27.en: * Let the warm south wind blow upon Your garden, that my soul may be filled with the warmth of the Spirit.

37.23.28.en: And my heart may burn with Your holy zeal!

37.23.29.en: If You permit the cold north wind to blow upon me; if You permit trials to surround me, I am confident in the riches of Your love and wisdom.

37.23.30.en: You who move nature in all its greatness for my sake, how can I not trust Your good ordering of my whole life?!
